evidence: owner.lisp:2685-2686 (inside the fnn-owner-serialized thunk) `(:bootstrap (multiple-value-bind (history incarnation) (fnn-owner-consumer-entropy-observation) ...` → owner.lisp:2663 `(with-open-file (input "/dev/urandom" :direction :input :element-type '(unsigned-byte 8)) ...)`. Topic install likewise calls `(fnn-csprng-octets 32 "topic installed ID")` inside the quantum (2640). The SASL seed comment at 564-567 states the design: 'The seed is read from the OS CSPRNG off the owner mutex'.
fix: Take the 64 octets with fnn-csprng-octets before fnn-owner-serialized (as fnn-owner-sasl-seed does) and pass them into the thunk. Do the same for the topic installed ID.
reviewer: fnn-owner-consumer-entropy-observation (2660-2669) opens /dev/urandom with with-open-file inside the fnn-owner-serialized thunk (2683-2688). It bypasses fnn-csprng-octets (io.lisp:880), including that function's fnn-test-entropy hook. That is real duplication and inconsistent with the SASL seed's off-mutex rule (564-567). However, /dev/urandom does not block after boot and the cost is one open/read/close on a rare local-control bootstrap, so the stall impact is negligible. Topic install also calls fnn-csprng-octets under the mutex (2640).
scenario: Each consumer bootstrap opens a file, allocates a Lisp stream and reads under the semantic critical section, which stalls every queued reader and transit quantum for an open(2)+read(2)+close(2). On a host where /dev/urandom is unavailable or blocks (a chroot or early boot), the owner mutex is held for the duration. The read also bypasses the fnn-csprng-octets primitive that every other entropy observation uses, so the two paths can diverge in error classification.
title: Consumer bootstrap reads /dev/urandom through a CL file stream while holding the owner mutex
